Group sizes are drawn at random around the mean, here 4, 3, 3, and 2, then 5, 4, and 3, then 6, 5, and 1, so a larger mean gives fewer, bigger groups; edges are dense inside a group and sparse between groups." width="100%"} Splits `n` nodes into groups whose sizes are drawn from a normal distribution with mean `mean_size` and variance `mean_size / shape`, rounded to whole numbers, and then joins each pair of nodes at random: with probability `p_in` if they are in the same group and with probability `p_out` if they are not. Sizes below `1` are redrawn, and the last group is cut short so that the sizes add up to exactly `n`. This is the benchmark of Brandes, Gaertler, and Wagner (2003); NetworkX has the same model as `gaussian_random_partition_graph()`. Each node's group (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, so the planted communities can be compared with what a detection method finds. The groups are created in order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In an undirected graph each pair is joined at most once and edges point from the earlier-created node to the later one; in a directed graph each ordered pair is drawn separately. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Gaussian random partition graphs are useful for: - benchmarking community detection when the number and sizes of the communities are not known in advance - generating many random test graphs with similar but not identical group structure - studying how methods cope with a mix of small and large groups ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes. Must be non-negative. [mean_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean group size. Must be at least `1`. [shape]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Controls how much the group sizes vary: the variance is `mean_size / shape`, so larger values give more equal sizes. Must be positive. [p_in]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in the same group, between `0` and `1`. [p_out]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in different groups, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator, used for both the sizes and the edges. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's group. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative, `mean_size=` is less than `1`, `shape=` is not positive, or `p_in=` or `p_out=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `200` nodes in groups of about `20`: ::: {#1a23e186 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_gaussian_random_partition_graph( n=200, mean_size=20, shape=2, p_in=0.3, p_out=0.01, seed=5 ) graph.get_node_df()["community"].value_counts().sort("community")["count"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [20, 24, 19, 17, 22, 14, 19, 23, 16, 20, 6] ``` ::: ::: A larger `shape=` makes the sizes more uniform: ::: {#2f163f4a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} even = ec.Graph().add_gaussian_random_partition_graph( n=200, mean_size=20, shape=50, p_in=0.3, p_out=0.01, seed=5 ) even.get_node_df()["community"].value_counts().sort("community")["count"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [20, 21, 20, 19, 20, 19, 20, 21, 19, 20, 1] ``` ::: :::
